tasks.title: Top three
tasks.statement: Write a function top3(nums): a list of the three largest elements in descending order. If there are fewer than three elements, return as many as there are. The original list must not be changed: use sorted, not sort.
tasks.hint: sorted(nums, reverse=True)[:3] -- the slice is safe for short lists too.

tasks.title: By word length
tasks.statement: Write a function by_length(words): a new list of the words sorted by length from shortest to longest. Words of the same length keep their original order. Use the key parameter.
tasks.hint: sorted(words, key=len) -- the sort is stable: words of equal length are not reordered.

tasks.title: Word lengths
tasks.statement: Write a function word_lengths(words): a list of the word lengths in the same order. Write it in one line, with a list comprehension.

tasks.title: Squares of the even ones
tasks.statement: Write a function even_squares(nums): a list of the squares of only the even elements, in the original order. Use a single list comprehension with a condition.
tasks.hint: [x * x for x in nums if x % 2 == 0] -- the if goes after the for.

tasks.title: Are all even
tasks.statement: Write a function all_even(nums): True if all elements are even, otherwise False. For an empty list, return True. Try the built-in function all.
tasks.hint: return all(x % 2 == 0 for x in nums).

tasks.title: No repeats, in order
tasks.statement: Write a function unique_sorted(nums): a list sorted in ascending order with no repeats: [3, 1, 3, 2, 1] becomes [1, 2, 3]. Do not use sets (set) yet: pick the new elements with an in check.
tasks.hint: if x not in seen: seen.append(x); at the end seen.sort() and return seen.

tasks.title: Brackets in order
tasks.statement: Write a function balanced(s): True if the round brackets in the string s are placed correctly: every "(" has its own ")" to the right, and no ")" stands before its pair. Ignore all other characters. Use a list as a stack: append on "(", pop on ")".
tasks.hint: On ")" first check that the stack is not empty: if it is empty, there is nothing to close -- return False right away (otherwise pop fails with an error).

tasks.title: Second largest
tasks.statement: Write a function second_largest(nums): the second largest DISTINCT value in a list of at least two different numbers: for [3, 1, 4, 1, 5] it is 4, for [10, 10, 5] it is 5.
tasks.hint: Remove the repeats (as in unique_sorted), sort, and take the next to last: items[-2].
